new_codes.help_title: That column cannot be read as dates
new_codes.help_text: The column chosen as the date each row describes does not exist, or its cells cannot be read as dates without guessing whether the day or the month comes first. Pick a column whose cells read as dates. A column with dates on only some rows can still be picked, but the rows without a date are counted and you are asked how to split them.

new_codes.help_title: This goal has no training time to choose
new_codes.help_text: This goal's learner (an uplift model on LightGBM) takes no time limit, so Quick, Balanced and Thorough are not offered. Training takes as long as the learner needs.

final.dec_text:
DEC-1814 (Plan O M244) - time settings, owned by Data Doctor.
(a) The training budget comes as three plain choices, never a raw minutes field: Quick, Balanced (recommended, where similar past runs stopped finding better models) and Thorough. Each says "about N min" and what it buys. Inputs are rows x columns x the model families the goal allows x this deployment's past runs (the stage durations M189 stores). With no runs, the public library's runs are the prior, the estimate says "from similar public datasets", and Balanced is `check`, not `sure`.
(b) One computation for the setting and the promise. Guided setup's advisor is the path that writes model_search.time_limit_minutes. Behind the switch it gets the deployment's store (AgentContext.run_history, passed only by api/routes/agent.py) and works the budget out on past runs. It keeps that same offer beside the file. A caller with no store says only "Estimated from similar public datasets." and claims nothing about runs it did not read.
(c) Offers are kept per file and goal, newest first (at most 20; the same choices offered again are kept once). A run whose limit matches any kept choice is promised exactly that choice's expectation, so the first ETA equals the promise even after a newer run moves the next offer. A limit set any other way on offered data is promised estimate() of that limit, from the same history and the offer's file (choice `custom`, "Your own time limit (about N min)"). A run on data with no offer keeps M189's estimate.
(d) After each run, actual against expected is recorded per stage (time_record.json). The next estimates correct each stage by the median actual-over-base of the last ten records, clamped to 0.5-2.
(e) The as-of date is decided (`sure`) only when the goal or its settings name it, or the person chose it.
    - A candidate must read as dates and have a date on at least 95% of all rows; the outcome column never is one.
    - A sparse date column is listed in `left_out` with the reason. When its filled rows are at least half yes and twice the file's rate, the reason says it is the outcome's own date.
    - Being the only date column is a question, never a decision.
(f) Cut points use the split's own rule. Rows with no date are counted (`undated_rows`), named in the sentence, and make TIME_CUTS a question. Infeasible cuts become an automatic "split at random". Feasible cuts are AUTO only with no undated rows and no part too small.
(g) Every answered time question's item names its `setting` (training_budget, cuts, label_maturity, snapshot_cadence) and carries the change itself:
    - the budget and the split answers are `setting` items (path and value);
    - "Leave it out" carries `after` (the cut-off) and the remove_rows `step`;
    - the cadence carries `spec_path` snapshots.frequency.
    time_setting_changes reads them back; apply_time_settings replays the steps with run_recipe.
(h) An effect payload may list keys under `per_file`; standing.meaning_of leaves them out. A standing "Leave it out" therefore applies next month with next month's cut-off instead of asking again. No existing effect uses per_file, so other meanings are unchanged.
(i) With data_doctor.unified off, nothing here runs: _time_rules, every budget and M189's progress bar are byte-identical.
final.readme_note: M244 time settings (Plan O, DEC-1814), behind data_doctor.unified. Training time is offered as Quick / Balanced (recommended) / Thorough, each "about N min", estimated from this deployment's past runs. Before any run exists it says "from similar public datasets". Guided setup suggests Balanced and keeps the offer it showed, so the progress bar's first ETA equals the promise. Data Doctor also proposes the date each row describes, where a split by date cuts, whether the newest rows' outcomes are final yet, and how often to take snapshots. A sparse outcome date is never taken as the date each row describes. Answers are kept as the change itself and remembered per client.
cross_branch: To M243 (prescription): time answers are case items whose payload `setting` is one of training_budget, cuts, label_maturity or snapshot_cadence. The budget and the split answers are kind `setting` (path and value), which your _section already reads into SettingChoice. "Leave it out" (LABEL_MATURITY) is kind `time_setting` and carries `step`, a remove_rows `after` RecipeStep dump, on item.upload_id; your build reads `step` from any accepted item, so it is already applied. engine.doctor.time_settings.time_setting_changes(case, goal_id) returns all of them as TimeChanges(settings, steps, spec), and apply_time_settings(frame, changes, upload_id=, config=) replays the steps with run_recipe. Until the prescription's prepared copy exists, VERIFY (readiness_verify) reads the stored upload, so X_LABEL_MATURITY still fails there after "Leave it out". It passes once the prepared copy is replayed (shown in test_time_settings_visit).

To M237 (build): the SNAPSHOT_CADENCE answer's item carries spec_path `snapshots.frequency` and value monthly or weekly (time_settings.SNAPSHOT_SPEC_PATH). It is returned in TimeChanges.spec for the DatasetSpec the build uses.

To M246 (standing answers, engine/doctor/standing.py): _without_ids, and so meaning_of, now leaves out the keys an effect payload lists under `per_file` (standing.PER_FILE_KEY), plus `per_file` itself. Only M244's LABEL_MATURITY 'leave_out' uses it (per_file: after, step). Every existing effect's meaning is unchanged.

To every AgentContext builder: engine/agent/tools.AgentContext has a new optional field `run_history: Storage | None = None`. Only api/routes/agent.py (Guided setup) passes the store. No tool reads it; advisor._training_budget reads it only while data_doctor.unified is on.

To M241 (test_header_switch_unified): the switch-on goldens now pin M244's training-time suggestion per case in tests/fixtures/agent_bench/expected_time_budget_on.json. Every other entry of each digest must still equal expected.json, and every switch-off digest of the unchanged cases must equal expected.json.
final.notes:
Every review issue was fixed, so none is rejected.

Major 1 (the advisor and the promise from one computation):
- AgentContext has a new optional field, run_history, and api/routes/agent.py passes the store.
- advisor._training_budget computes propose_budget(time_inputs(store, ...)) once, saves that offer for the upload and use case, and passes it to recommend_settings(training_budget=...).
- Offers are now a TimeOffers log, newest first, capped at 20, with the same choices kept once. read_offer returns the newest and read_offers returns all.
- promised_tracker searches every kept offer. When no choice matches the run's limit, it falls back to estimate() from the same history on the offer's file (choice `custom`).
- With no store, propose_budget's reason says only "Estimated from similar public datasets." (TimeInputs.from_store).
- New test: four past runs -> advise() -> accept the proposal through run_overrides -> run -> first eta_seconds == the offered Balanced expected_seconds.
- A Guided-setup session now writes uploads/<id>/time_offers/<use case>.json, but only when the switch is on.

Major 2 (sparse outcome date):
- _as_of requires a date on at least 95% of all rows and excludes the outcome column.
- A sparse column goes into AsOf.left_out with the reason. If it is the outcome's own date, the reason says so.
- The only-readable-column rule no longer sets sure; it becomes a question.
- When the person picks a sparse column anyway, it is honoured: _cuts counts undated_rows and puts them in the sentence, and TIME_CUTS becomes an unproven question.
- The reviewer's fixture (30,000 rows, cancelled_on filled only where the outcome is yes, about 10% of rows) now gives no as-of column, cancelled_on in left_out, the question, and no TIME_CUTS ask.

Major 3 (time answers are applied):
- The payloads of the four time asks now carry the change (see dec_text g).
- The split answers changed from kind time_setting to kind setting so the run's configuration carries them.
- New in time_settings.py: time_setting_changes and apply_time_settings.
- New in standing.py: the per_file convention (see dec_text h).
- The visit test answers "Leave it out" through visit.answer, builds the prepared copy from the case and asserts X_LABEL_MATURITY passes. Next month's file is shifted one month; the standing answer applies with cut-off 2026-09-30 instead of 2026-08-31 and asks nothing.

Design decision for the integrator: "Leave it out" stays kind `time_setting`. Its `step` is a remove_rows step, but the design makes LABEL_MATURITY a standing time setting, so it is not raised to the APPROVE-class remove_rows rule.

Tests changed, none loosened:
- test_a_custom_budget_not_among_the_choices_keeps_m189s_estimate is replaced by ..._is_promised_the_estimate_from_the_same_history, which asserts the exact ETA as the review asks. M189's estimate is still covered by a new test, test_a_run_on_data_no_offer_was_made_for_keeps_m189s_estimate.
- test_an_event_file_offers_monthly_or_weekly_snapshots now passes as_of_column and also asserts that the undecided case is a question.
- The random-split payload assertion now includes setting=cuts.

M241's switch-on goldens: the original M244 commit already broke 34 of them, because the switch-on time suggestion is now Balanced (for example 6, check) instead of the file-size rule's 10 (sure). In every case that was the only difference in the digest. The test now pins the M244 entry per case in a recorded fixture, and the rest of each digest still has to equal expected.json exactly.

The AI cassette was re-recorded from the offline reference model; no network or key is needed.

Two failures are not caused by M244 (they also fail on HEAD~1): test_hardening viewer, and test_eval_harness pass5 for preflight and check_uplift_data, which fails when run alone. The untracked .m244_tests.log in the worktree is not committed.

issues.where: engine/agent/recommend.py _budget_rules (about lines 345-375); engine/agent/advisor.py:1617 (the only caller of recommend_settings, which never passes training_budget); engine/doctor/time_settings.py promised_tracker (about 1114-1160) and time_settings_detector save_offer (about 1870-1885)
issues.problem: The setup advisor is the only path that actually writes model_search.time_limit_minutes into a run's config, and it always works from the public-library prior. It never calls time_inputs(None, ...) with a store, and it never saves an offer. The rest of the feature uses the deployment's history: the detector and propose_training_budget estimate from past runs and save the offer that promised_tracker matches by exact minutes. Three things follow once a deployment has finished runs. (1) The advisor's Balanced minutes differ from the minutes in the saved offer. promised_tracker then finds no matching choice, and the ETA quietly falls back to M189's estimate, so the screen and the promise disagree. That is the core requirement of (a). (2) The advisor's reason text says 'Estimated from similar public datasets: there is no finished training run here to go by yet.' That is false whenever runs exist, so the advisor states a basis it does not have. (3) The detector rewrites the offer on every detect pass. A budget the person already accepted (say 15 min) stops matching once a newer run changes the history (Balanced becomes 18). The ETA test passes only because it builds the config by hand from the offer's minutes, so it never goes through a path that sets the value.
issues.fix: Give the advisor a store. Pass training_budget=propose_budget(time_inputs(storage, config, rows=..., columns=...)) into recommend_settings, and save the same offer for that upload and use case, so the setting and the offer come from one computation. In promised_tracker, when no offered choice matches the run's limit, fall back to estimate(time_inputs(ctx.storage, config, rows, columns, exclude_run_id=run_id), minutes) and promise that, so any chosen budget still gets an ETA from the same source. Keep earlier offers instead of overwriting them: append, or key them by minutes, so an accepted choice stays matchable. When _budget_rules has no store, say only 'estimated from similar public datasets'. Never claim that no run exists here. Add a test that goes advisor proposal → accepted setting → run → first eta_seconds == the offered choice's expected_seconds, with a history of at least 3 runs.

issues.problem: A column becomes an as-of candidate when at least 95% of its FILLED cells read as dates, and its fill rate is never checked. If it is the only such column, it is taken as 'sure' ('the only column that reads as dates'). The cut points are then computed on the rows that have a date, with every other row silently dropped, and feasible cuts are accepted automatically (proven='dates'). I reproduced this with the fault-prediction config on a 30,000-row file whose only date column is a 10%-filled outcome date ('cancelled_on', filled only for positives). Result: as_of=cancelled_on with sure=True, and the cuts say 'Testing uses the 456 rows from 2025-09-14 on...' with validation_positives == validation_rows and test_positives == test_rows. The ask was TIME_CUTS with proven='dates', so it was accepted without a question. That is a time split on an outcome-event date: the test set is defined by the outcome itself, which leaks it. The row counts the person sees also leave out 27,000 rows. The question is not asked even though the rules cannot be sure.
issues.fix: In _as_of, require a candidate to be filled on nearly every row: count non-null parsed dates against len(frame), with the same READABLE_SHARE threshold. Exclude the target or outcome column, and any column that is filled mostly on positive rows. Never return sure=True from the 'only readable column' rule; leave it as an AS_OF_COLUMN question unless the goal or config names the column. In _cuts, say how many rows have no date and are not placed, and do not mark the cuts proven when undated rows exist. Add a fixture test with a sparse outcome-date column that must produce a question and no automatically accepted TIME_CUTS.

issues.where: engine/doctor/time_settings.py time_settings_asks LABEL_MATURITY 'leave_out' effect (about 1735-1760); TIME_CUTS 'random' and 'dates' effects; no consumer anywhere in engine/ or api/ (grep finds no reader of 'time_setting' items, maturity_step or leave_out_immature outside tests)
issues.problem: Answering the time questions only records a case item; nothing applies it. 'Leave it out' adds a kind='time_setting' item whose payload is {setting, choice, column, window_days}. It does not carry the cutoff date (maturity.immature_from). When immaturity was detected from the yes-rate rather than from a window, window_days is None, so the item cannot even be turned back into the rows to drop. No step leaves the immature rows out, so the acceptance 'leaving it out makes X_LABEL_MATURITY pass' holds only in a unit test that calls leave_out_immature() directly. The same gap applies to 'Split at random' / 'Test on the newest dates' and the cadence answer. They are also stored as standing answers and re-applied next month as pre-ticked items that change nothing, which tells the person something happened when nothing did.
issues.fix: Put the change itself into the effect payload. For leave_out, include 'after': maturity.immature_from and the replayable step (maturity_step(column, immature_from).model_dump()), so M243's prescription or the hand-off can apply it. Recompute the cutoff when a standing answer is re-applied to next month's file. Say in the result's cross_branch notes which milestone consumes 'time_setting' items. Add an acceptance test that answers LABEL_MATURITY with leave_out through visit.answer, builds the prepared copy from the case, and asserts X_LABEL_MATURITY passes.

reviews.verdict: Not ready: 3 majors, 0 blockers. Switch-off parity holds, lint is clean (ruff and black), no forbidden shared docs were edited, the builder's log reports 1447 passed, and the questions go through M246's settle with per-client standing answers. But (1) the advisor, the only path that sets the training time limit, works from the public prior with no saved offer and wrongly says there are no past runs, so once a deployment has history the ETA does not match the promise; (2) a sparse outcome-date column can be taken as the as-of date for sure, and a leaking time split is then accepted without asking; (3) answered time settings (leave out the newest month, the split choice) are recorded but never applied, and the leave-out payload lacks the cutoff date.
